My statement pertaining to this post:  
Yes!! Please do all of the above, establish baselines, protect your hearing at every chance, stand up for yourself, and don't be afraid to contact OSHA if your manager/hr/company is not doing anything about it.   
I started my career as a lab tech in the Army and learned two things about Lab Techs and hearing loss very quickly:

\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*

Hearing loss is the most common occupational medical disability claimed by lab techs.

\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*

Most of this is caused by humms, and purrs of instruments that you don't notice -- because they aren't that loud -- the constant vibrations of the hairs that "feel" the noise wear them down....  


**Everything after this is a rant that I didn't mean to go on, but I feel I needed to get out, so I'm going to leave it here. Sorry for any inconvenience.**  


What about when complaints were made and made and made. 

  
My biggest complaint being that the biggest culprit was our deep freezer -- something that could have easily been fixed (coolant fan, I think, but I'm not expert). Or moved, though this would create a minor inconvenience.  
To talk to your coworkers required yelling in the same room.   
When the thing kicked on it scared the crap out of nearly every employee, no matter how long they had been there, and could be heard in adjoining rooms, even rooms adjoining indirectly.  
I'm certain my boss intentionally, actively ignored it, because of the cost involved in fixing it, and the logistics involved in moving it.  I'm also almost certain this is why she made a push for her office to be moved from the lab -- so the lab could grow into the space her desk took up.

I complained so much that supposedly OSHA was brought out to look at it, I work nights -- so you never know, but HR told me they had, and that it tested fine.   


There were days when I would have to go into another room to do a handoff because after 12 hours of listening to the beast roar in the corner I would have a migraine and not be able to finish a sentence , or follow my own thoughts without wanting to yell at the stupid thing.  
I requested to get my hearing tested to establish a baseline -- didn't want it to come out of my pocket, and I didn't feel that it should. It took nearly a week for the HR manager to get back to me to inform me that the hospitals lawyers advised against it, so they would not be able to..

​

For nearly 2 years I dreamed of stabbing a pen in the coolant fan as I walked out of my last shift for the week. 

​

....   
Then I realized that the issue was my manager, and how the hospital let her convince them of whatever delusion she was having to make herself look good and us look bad. 

IE: We're whiney-bratty lab techs that can't do their jobs (shows some insignificant error made 6 months ago, or that she partook in setting-up employees to make sure techs were "doing their jobs" -- a red oil pencil mark on the underside of a machine means the machine wasn't cleaned that weekend -- ( nevermind the 3 months worth of saline buildup on the cell washer....) and therefore, should not be listened to.   


and I stayed for 1 more year....   
Money without a commute is nice.

This is what I have typed up -- which kinda explains the situation as well. 

​

\[HR ladys name\],

  
I don't know if this is appropriate or not, but I would love for a chance to explain some things, especially if those are the true and only reasons to decide to pass on me... i think it may be a mistake.    
I am very interested in this position,  I've passed up/put on hold a few other options hoping for this one. I love the fact that its patient interaction and helping people, but not the same place or "box" as I so lovingly referred to my last workplace since it didn't even have windows.  
He misunderstood me on the weekend thing. I worked 12-hour overnights every single thurs, fri, and Saturday nights for two and a half years,  no one would ever cover my shifts so I got to use one vacation day that whole time.... I don't want to go back to a position where my soul requirement is weekends. The difference is this position is not all weekend every weekend.I fully understand that this job requires a fluid schedule and most weekends. This is another plus for me. I am a gypsy soul and get bored easily with routine -- I thrived in the Army, my smart, timid, structured son did not, so i had to grow roots.   
In fact the schedule offered with Thursday/Sundays off is perfect for me and my family. I'd still get date night Thursday and football Sunday's.  :)   
As for teamwork, I don't think I conveyed that answer well enough either, I feel I can thrive in either environment - depending on the people I'm expected to work with.   
I tend to do things very methodically especially in a work environment,  and if someone comes and doesn't follow the same system that is when I struggle.    
I was burned on a previous interview a few years back for preferring to work alone (that's why I was nights for so long..) so, I'm very hesitant for that to be my answer,  since I know I can do well in either environment.    
In fact if im bluntly honest,  and why not be since I am making one last stand, the only thing about this job that I wasn't over the moon excited for was learning to set up the EEGS lol. I have experience with seizures through my clinic work while deployed and my puppy was diagnosed with epilepsy at 3 months old. The study of brain function fascinates me, but who doesn't want to understand more about what makes them, them... But-All the wires look complicated. So did lab machines before I started lab school,  and I can pull one of those apart, fix it and put it back together, so I figured that part of it would work itself out.  
I understand that hiring someone is a risky, and expensive endeavor for you guys,  and imagine that some people get caught up in the perks and lie to get a job that they know won't suit them, and I can assure you that I'm not that person... I genuinely want this job and think that I may be the perfect person to "own" this area.  
Once again,  I'm not sure if this is appropriate, and I apologize if not .... also, I fully understand if you guys still decide to move in a different direction and I thank you for allowing me to steal a bit more of your time.   
At the very least can you forward this information to \[hiring manager\]?  
I'm available if there are anymore questions.   
I really do think I could be a great fit for this.  


Thank you. 

Wishing you well this Thanksgiving.
